Graph evidence revealed the transaction originated from a rare new device profile (Windows | other | chrome 61.0 | 1280x720) that was recently used on two other customers' cards. The final actions taken were BLOCK_CARD, CREATE_CASE, FILE_REPORT, and MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS.

sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details a confirmed card-not-present fraud incident involving customer C07987 and card C07987-K2. On 2016-12-01 at 17:28:53, an online transaction of $99.92 (ID 3503878) was attempted using the card. The transaction was flagged because it originated from a device profile (Windows | other | chrome 61.0 | 1280x720) marked as new for this account. While the amount of $99.92 is typical for the customer and resembles a recurring monthly charge, the device anomaly prompted further investigation. Network analysis showed this specific, rare device profile was used on two other cards (C06224-K2, C11309-K1) belonging to different customers between 2016-11-29 and 2016-12-01. The bank contacted the customer via step-up authentication, and the cardholder confirmed they still possessed the card and did not authorize the transaction. This confirms a card-not-present fraud pattern from a new device, indicating compromised card details. The total exposure for this case is $99.92. Consequently, the bank blocked the card, created a case, filed this report, and initiated monitoring on the connected cards.
